additions.reason: The Shechina (Divine Presence) is central to this Torah — it dwells in the west (שכינה במערב), weeps over Israel, and is explicitly equated with the Kotel Ma'aravi. It is a bechina of the holy light/presence that the Tzaddik embodies. The Torah says 'השכינה בוכה ומיללת... בחינת רחל מבכה על בניה' — the Shechina IS Rachel weeping, and this is the same essential nature as the west and the concealment of the eye-light. The Shechina belongs in Package 1 as the divine indwelling presence whose weeping = the setting of holy light.
additions.source_quote: כִּי שְׁכִינָה בְּמַעֲרָב (ב"ב כה), וְהַשְּׁכִינָה בּוֹכָה וּמְיַלֶּלֶת, כִּבְיָכוֹל, עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, בְּחִינַת: רָחֵל מְבַכָּה עַל בָּנֶיהָ

additions.reason: Rachel (the matriarch) appears multiple times in this Torah as a bechina of the Shechina weeping in exile. The Torah says 'מערב — ראשי תיבות: רחל מבכה על בניה' — the west IS Rachel weeping. Rachel also IS Yosef's mother, connecting her to the Tzaddik-as-Yosef theme. At the end of the Torah, the Rebbe explicitly calls Rachel 'עולמתא שפירתא דלית לה עיינין' — the beautiful maiden without eyes — in her exile state. Rachel is a bechina of the Shechina, the west, and the weeping/concealment reality.

additions.reason: The Torah repeatedly states that the four letters of God's Name (the Tetragrammaton) are a bechina of the four elements, the four mochin, and the three colors of the eye plus the pupil. 'שמו יתברך — הוא בחינת ארבע אותיות השם... ולמטה נשתלשל מבחינת הארבעה יסודות.' This node is a key structural pivot connecting שם ה, the four elements, and the eye-colors — all in Package 1.

additions.reason: The Torah enumerates the four mochin explicitly: חכמה, תבונה, דעת, וכל מלאכה — and says these are the four mochin (citing Tikkunei Zohar). They emerge from the four letters of God's Name and then produce the three colors of the eye. This is a distinct node from the general 'מחין' already in the dataset — the Torah specifically calls them 'ארבעה מחין' and they are a key structural link in the chain: שם ה → ארבע אותיות → ארבעה מחין → תלת גונין דעינא. Belongs in Package 1.

additions.reason: Bezalel is explicitly called a bechina of the Tzaddik in this Torah: 'ראו כי קרא ה' בשם בצלאל — ראו דייקא, כי על ידי שנתגלה ונתגדל שם בצלאל, עליידי זה ראו... כי ה' הוא בשם בצלאל, כי שמו משותף בשמנו.' Bezalel's name containing God's name, and the opening of eyes through his renown, makes him a bechina of the Tzaddik whose name = God's name. Belongs in Package 1 alongside צדיק האמת / ראש בית.

additions.reason: Rising at midnight (חצות) is the prescribed practice this Torah urges — mourning over the Temple at midnight. The Rebbe says 'צריך לזהר מאד לקום בחצות, ולהיות מתאבל על חרבן בית המקדש.' Midnight is the time when the holy side can overcome the fire-lights through mourning. It is a bechina of the turning point between domination of מאורי אש and the restoration of מאורי אור. While not given explicit bechina language, it is thematically essential to the gap between the two packages.

The node 'המחין' and 'מחין' are treated as distinct node IDs in the dataset. In the Torah text they likely refer to the same concept (the intellect), but since they are separate node_id entries, they are kept separate in the package assignment.

The Torah's dominant structural chain is: שם ה → ארבע אותיות → ארבעה מחין → תלת גונין דעינא ובת עין → מאור העינים → כח הראות / כלליות הגונין. This chain descends from divine unity to the physical act of seeing.

The Torah's argument: The true Tzaddik (= שבת = שם ה = ראש בית) brings holy light/vision into the world. When he is revealed, eyes open. When a false leader (מפרסמים של שקר) is exalted, God's name is hidden, holy light withdraws, and fire-lights (מאורי אש) grow — burning the Temple. The eitza chain runs: [Pkg 1] → [Pkg 3 false leadership causes] → [Pkg 2 fire-lights grow] → destruction. Mourning at midnight (חצות) reverses this by suppressing fire-lights and restoring holy light.

The עולמתא שפירתא דלית לה עיינין (the beautiful maiden without eyes) is a Zoharic phrase the Rebbe applies to Rachel in exile — she IS the Shechina without her eye-light (מאור עינים departed). This phrase could be an additional node bridging the Rachel/Shechina/eye-light cluster.
